title: Causal Reasoning Foundations
purpose: Seed conservative causal reasoning so Lantern distinguishes association from causation, represents direction, confounding, mediation and intervention, and requires appropriate evidence before promoting causal claims.

concepts.definition: A factor whose intervention/presence makes a difference to an outcome under a specified causal model and scope; exact semantics depend on causal framework.
An outcome causally influenced by one or more factors under a declared model/scope.
The directed relationship from cause toward effect; association alone does not identify direction.
A directed graph representing hypothesized causal relationships among variables under explicit assumptions.
A variable that causally influences two or more variables and can induce association between them.
A variable related causally to both exposure/treatment and outcome such that failing to account for it can distort causal inference.
A variable lying on a causal pathway through which some effect of X on Y operates.
A variable causally influenced by two or more variables; conditioning on it can create spurious association.
A deliberate setting/manipulation of a variable distinguished from merely observing its value.
An outcome considered under an alternative intervention/condition for the same conceptual unit/world; not directly jointly observable in ordinary settings.
Within a declared scope/model, an outcome does not occur without the factor; necessity does not imply sufficiency.
Within a declared scope/model, the factor/condition is enough to produce the outcome; sufficiency does not imply necessity.
A contributing factor that participates in causal production without being necessary or sufficient alone.
An intermediate process explaining how a cause produces or influences an effect; evidence for mechanism can strengthen but is not always required for causal inference.
A cause must precede or be appropriately temporally related to its effect; precedence alone does not establish causation.
Systematic change in outcome with exposure level can support causal interpretation under suitable conditions but is neither necessary nor sufficient by itself.
An observed association attributed to X causing Y when Y actually causes or influences X.

guards.reason: Association alone does not establish causal direction or exclude confounding.
Temporal precedence is necessary in many causal settings but not sufficient.
Post hoc ordering alone is not causal evidence.
Association does not determine either causal direction.
A plausible mechanism is supportive context, not proof that the causal effect occurs.
Necessary and sufficient conditions are distinct.
Controlling a mediator can remove part of the causal effect being estimated; adjustment depends on the estimand/question.
Conditioning on a collider can introduce spurious association.
Observing a value and intervening to set it can have different causal implications.
A causal graph represents a model/hypothesis unless supported by evidence.
Causal effects can depend on population, conditions, dose, time and environment.

invariants: Association, prediction and causation are distinct claim types.
Causal direction must be represented explicitly.
Causal claims carry scope and model assumptions.
Observing X is not automatically equivalent to intervening on X.
Potential confounders, mediators and colliders play different roles and must not be adjusted indiscriminately.
Necessary and sufficient causes are distinct; many real causes are contributing/component causes.
Temporal precedence alone is insufficient for causation.
Causal graphs are models/hypotheses with provenance, not truth declarations.
Interventional evidence can strengthen causal inference when comparison and confounding assumptions are justified.
Causal conclusions preserve the evidence/methodology chain that licensed them.
A causal effect established in one scope does not automatically generalize universally.

provenance.authoring_basis: Foundational causal inference concepts, directed causal reasoning and intervention/observational distinctions adapted to Lantern's bounded Schema-v3 and methodology architecture.
